# LaunchLoom progress update - 2026-10-22

## New-niche model trial results (2026-10-22T14:18:16Z)

- Intake issue #179 (Kestrel & Rye Coffee Roasters, fictional hospitality QA)
  selected three distinct reference families for the restaurant niche:
  typographic-poster (Leon's), archive-rail (Tavola), market-collage (Ethos).
  This differs from the recent plumbing trio (utility-diagnostic plus two
  typographic-poster references) and the beauty trio (editorial-monument plus
  two cinematic-stage references). The generated recipe was `general-editorial`
  / `general-bold-launch`, a third direction next to `local-trades` and
  `care-editorial`.
- Trial A (GLM-5.3, run 39674472669): Reference DNA passed on Go, but authoring
  failed on all three routes with upstream provider faults; no candidates or
  preview. GLM-5.3 is not viable for the authoring contract in this slice.
- Trial B (DeepSeek v4-pro, run 39676750388): authoring passed and a preview
  was delivered, but the rendered reference judge truncated at 24k repeatedly
  and the repair budget exhausted. The design is visually distinct from the
  DeepSeek flash control (minimal line-art, no retained images), while the
  recipe and variant were identical (`general-editorial` /
  `general-bold-launch`): the intake/reference choice sets the design family,
  the model changes execution, not the family.
- Control (DeepSeek v4.1 flash, run 39674491249): authoring passed and a
  preview was delivered (https://e695581d.launchloom-pipeline-preview.pages.dev).
  The diversity judge truncated at 12k and the low-effort retry errored, so
  the run failed closed. Imagery at the six-request runtime budget kept one
  image; hero and secondary were both attempted per route (no hero
  starvation), tertiary remained request-budget-exhausted.
- Sameness diagnosis: the focused creative-only harness bypasses the
  history-aware selector and never records attempts, so the pack seed is the
  fixed intake submission ID and reruns of the same intake are deterministic.
  Beauty had 19 valid trios but always selected one; the plumbing niche had
  only one valid trio. Production uses a shared history worktree; the focused
  QA path does not, which explains the repeated look across recent reruns.
  Recommended follow-up: give creative-only dispatches an optional variant
  seed or history-aware selection rather than changing production determinism.
- Judge reliability fix: diversity completion ceiling 12k -> 32k, reference
  judge default 24k -> 48k (a ceiling, not a gate), and safe provider
  diagnostics in the judge retry/error path. 57 rendered-judge/visual tests
  and npm run check (416 files, 0 errors) pass. Re-running v4-pro on issue #179
  to validate a passing delivery and the restored nine-request image budget.

## v4-pro validation and nine-request allocation evidence (2026-10-22)

- Re-ran DeepSeek v4-pro on issue #179 at main dd316614 (run 39796487516) to
  validate the judge budget fix and the restored request budget. Authoring
  failed on all three routes on harness contracts: route-01 used forbidden
  inline styles, route-02 used an image source without a sealed image content
  token, and route-03 used an unsafe `#` href. No preview was delivered. The
  earlier v4-pro run also lost two of three candidates to sealed-content
  violations, so v4-pro is not a viable upgrade for this authoring contract;
  DeepSeek v4.1 flash remains the production model.
- The same run recorded generated-assets with generationRequests=9 and exactly
  three attempts per route: hero, secondary and tertiary each got one attempt
  (route-03 retained its tertiary image; the rest were rejected by the image
  reviewer). This is the intended coverage-first behavior at the approved
  budget and confirms the earlier six-request run only starved the tertiary
  because the runtime budget was wrong, not because of the allocation logic.
- Dispatched DeepSeek v4.1 flash on issue #179 (run 39806327237) as the final
  validation of the 32k/48k judge ceilings and the nine-request budget on a
  model that previously authored two valid candidates.

## Client directory polish and dossier side sheet

- UTC started: 2026-10-22.
- Branch/worktree: `codex/launchloom-admin-clients-polish` at `/home/maigreeks/projects/.worktrees/launchloom-admin-clients-polish`, based on `origin/main` `50dc335e`.
- Nifty: parent `olT2!MG3kq`; subtasks `U5ZsgCrRpM`, `1lCXEXSZIJ`, `!hsLnCFakO`.
- Intent: make the Clients directory feel like the Generations workspace. Reorganize the crowded search/filter area, improve directory hierarchy and row scannability, and replace the inline client dossier with the same accessible blurred side sheet used by generation attempts.
- Constraints: preserve existing client filters, pagination, focus restoration, attempt links, safe site links, auth contracts, and mobile usability. Do not invent client data or alter the server contract unless the UI requires it.

### Client directory implementation pass

- Rebuilt the Clients toolbar as one quiet search line with a primary `Search clients` action, a collapsed advanced-filter panel, and separated refresh/filter controls. The old always-open five-control filter grid is gone.
- Replaced the cramped inline dossier column with `ClientDossier`, rendered in the same native modal side sheet as `AttemptInspector`: right-edge alignment, full viewport height, blurred backdrop, scroll lock, Escape/backdrop close, focus trap and trigger focus restoration.
- Fixed the shared side-sheet defect exposed by the first visual pass: the sheet never received its open state and was translated off-screen (only a sliver visible on mobile). Both generation and client sheets now add `is-open` after `showModal()` and align flush right.
- Redesigned the directory as a four-column editorial table with client monograms, business/contact hierarchy, issue context, submitted date, inviting admin and a single Open action. On narrow screens it becomes stacked cards with labeled fields and no horizontal page scrolling.
- Visual evidence: desktop directory, expanded filters, right-side dossier at 1512x960; 390px and 320px directory cards and full-height dossier sheets. Screenshot review confirmed no truncated controls, no off-screen sheet, and no page-level horizontal overflow.
- Validation so far: `npm run check` 0 errors; `vitest` admin browser/view-model/api suite 61 passed; production `npm run build` passed. Final full browser rerun and production deployment remain.
- Final local pass: full admin browser suite 31 passed (including the new client modal, keyboard, mobile, focus-return and overlay bounds checks); admin browser/view-model/api suite 61 passed; `npm run check` reported 0 errors; `npm run build:admin` and production `npm run build` passed. The shared sheet fix was verified visually in the generation preview as well as the client dossier.
- Deployment and live verification remain before this task is closed.

## Legacy client label correction

- Live production review found four legacy accepted clients with no business or contact name. The first client pass therefore surfaced raw `submission:...` values as the visible label and in the dossier heading.

- Corrected `formatClientName` to prefer recorded business/contact identity, then the recorded email, and only then a short derived `Client <record-prefix>` label. The exact record id, invitation and submission ids remain in the dossier record details.

- The directory avoids duplicating the email in the contact column when it is already the primary identity (`Email only`), and the dossier subtitle no longer repeats the heading email. A unit test covers both email and id-only fallbacks.

- Worktree/branch: `launchloom-admin-clients-labels` / `codex/launchloom-admin-clients-labels`, based on `origin/main` `62916eac`.
